title: OKP Commitment (proposal)
description: A hold against a capacity offer, with an explicit expiry and a stated remedy for the case where it cannot be met. PROPOSAL 0.1-draft. This is not part of OKP v0.2, it is not ratified, and it is not stable to build against.

offer_ref.description: The offer_id this commitment was taken against. References are not resolved by this proposal.

state.description: held -> confirmed -> fulfilled or failed. released is a deliberate cancellation by either side; expired is a hold nobody confirmed.

window.description: The promised window. Must fall inside the offer's window.

expires_at.description: When an unconfirmed hold lapses and the units return to the site. Required in every state: a hold that does not expire is capacity nobody owns.

confirmed_at.description: Required once the state is confirmed, fulfilled or failed.

accountable_party.description: Who is answerable if this promise is not met. A legal entity, never an employee.

on_failure.description: What happens when the commitment cannot be met. Stated when the promise is made, not discovered afterwards.

remedy.description: 'none_stated' is representable on purpose. A site may promise nothing, and a consumer may then refuse the hold; what it may not do is leave the question unanswered.

notice_min_s.description: Seconds of notice the site undertakes to give before the window, once it knows it will miss. Zero means no undertaking.

notice_ref.description: Where that notice is sent. Absent means the requester polls.

requester_ref.description: Opaque token the caller supplies to correlate its own records. MUST NOT encode a name, account, email address, phone number or payment reference. This proposal carries no identity.

ext.description: Vendor extensions. Keys MUST be reverse-domain names controlled by the producer. A payment authorisation is referenced here under the payment protocol's own key.
